rows: Johnny, Cat on a Driftwood
Edward Weston photographed his cat Johnny sitting on a piece of driftwood in 1944. Weston, famous for sharp photographs of peppers and rocks, also took pictures of pets at his home in California.
What shapes does the driftwood make?
Geometric Abstraction
Pim van Os made this abstract photograph just after World War II, using shapes and shadows instead of recognizable objects. He was a pioneer of abstract photography in the Netherlands.
What shapes can you find? Do they look like anything?
Princess Margriet
This photograph shows Princess Margriet of the Netherlands in 1945, the year she was born in Canada. Her family had fled the German occupation.
Why was she born in Canada?
Clement Attlee
This portrait shows Clement Attlee, who became the British prime minister in 1945 after Winston Churchill. He led the country in rebuilding after the war.
What would you do first to rebuild after a war?
New York Celebrating the Surrender of Japan

Victor Jorgensen photographed New Yorkers celebrating the surrender of Japan on August 14, 1945. Confetti and paper fell from the windows of tall buildings, and the streets were full of cheering people.
How would you celebrate the end of a long war?
Safed Street
This photograph from 1946 shows a street in Safed, an old city in northern Israel known for its stone alleys. It comes from the PikiWiki archive of Israel.
What do you notice about the stone alley?
Fashion Model on the Edge of a Boat, Montego Bay
Toni Frissell photographed a fashion model on the edge of a boat as a man rows at Montego Bay, Jamaica, in 1946. She liked to shoot fashion outdoors in natural light.
Why is outdoor light good for photographs?
Brendan Bracken
Yousuf Karsh photographed Brendan Bracken, a British politician and close friend of Winston Churchill, in 1947. Bracken was an early backer of the Financial Times.
What does an adviser to a prime minister do?
Albert Einstein
Orren Jack Turner photographed Albert Einstein in 1947. The scientist's wild hair and thoughtful look became a symbol of genius.
What do you think he was thinking?
Panorama of Marovoay, Madagascar
Walter Kaudern photographed the town of Marovoay in Madagascar in 1947. The broad panorama shows rice fields and a river town.
What would life by a river and rice fields be like?
Pierre Balmain and Ruth Ford
Carl Van Vechten photographed the French fashion designer Pierre Balmain with the American actress Ruth Ford in 1947. Balmain was one of the top designers in Paris.
What does a fashion designer do?
Summer Under Water
This photograph from Weeki Wachee Springs in Florida in 1947 shows a mermaid performer underwater. The Florida roadside attraction featured women who performed in the clear spring.
How do mermaid performers breathe underwater?
Hoang Minh Dao's Family
This 1947 photograph shows a Vietnamese family, Hoang Minh Dao and his wife and children. Family portraits record people in a time of change.
What can a family photo tell you?
Fashion Model in a Tennis Outfit, Seated on a Wall
Toni Frissell photographed a fashion model in a tennis outfit sitting on a wall in 1947. Frissell often posed models doing sports.
How would you pose in sports clothes?
Mayor D'Atilly Presents Press Photographers' Diplomas

The Dutch National Archive photographed the mayor handing out diplomas to press photographers during the festive week of 1948 in Amsterdam. Press photographers came from around the world for the coronation of Queen Juliana.
Why would a mayor give photographers diplomas?
The Altalena on the Tel Aviv Coast
Robert Capa photographed the ship Altalena on a beach in Tel Aviv in June 1948. The ship, carrying weapons for an Israeli militia, was shelled and burned during a conflict.
Why would a ship be burned at sea?
Frank Harriott, Karl Priebe, Edward Atkinson, Tom Kemp
Carl Van Vechten photographed four men, Frank Harriott, Karl Priebe, Edward Atkinson and Tom Kemp, in 1948. Van Vechten photographed hundreds of artists and writers.
Why would a photographer make portraits of so many creative people?
Press Photographers in Festival Week
Willem van de Poll photographed press photographers from home and abroad during festival week in 1948. They shared one crowded scene with many cameras.
How many cameras can you count?
Mary Jane, Model
Toni Frissell photographed a model called Mary Jane in 1948. Her pictures were published in fashion magazines like Harper's Bazaar.
What does a fashion model do?
Tryall Plantation, Jamaica
Toni Frissell photographed the Tryall plantation house in Jamaica in 1948. The old house stands among palms and gardens.
What would you do in a house in the tropics?
Sculling Off Jamaica
Toni Frissell photographed a man sculling, or rowing with a single oar from the stern, in a boat off Jamaica in 1948. The water shines in the sun.
How do you steer a boat with just one oar?
Albert and Elsa Einstein in Caputh
Lotte Jacobi photographed Albert and Elsa Einstein at their summer house in Caputh, near Berlin. They left Germany in 1933, and the house was later taken.
Why would a family leave their home?
A Street in Peki'in
This 1949 photograph from the PikiWiki archive shows a street in Peki'in, a village in northern Israel. Villagers have lived there for centuries.
What do you see on the village street?
Fashion Models Floating in a Swimming Pool
Toni Frissell photographed fashion models floating in bathing suits in a swimming pool in 1949. The poses look like flowers on the water.
How would you arrange people in a pool picture?
Walking with Signs in a Civil Rights March
Willie Brown and Doug Stewart walk with signs in a civil rights march in 1950. Activists marched for equal treatment long before the big marches of the 1960s.
What would you put on a sign?
Jacqueline Kennedy
Toni Frissell photographed Jacqueline Kennedy in 1952 for Sports Illustrated. She would become First Lady of the United States in 1961.
What would it be like to become First Lady?
Jackie Bouvier and Jack Kennedy in Wedding Attire
Toni Frissell photographed Jacqueline Bouvier and John F. Kennedy in wedding attire with members of the wedding party in Newport, Rhode Island, on September 12, 1953. Kennedy was a senator then.
What do you notice about the formal clothes?
Jackie and Jack Kennedy's Wedding
Toni Frissell photographed the bride and groom in Newport, Rhode Island, in 1953. About 800 guests came to the wedding.
Why would so many guests come?
The Newlyweds Talking at the Wedding
Toni Frissell photographed Jacqueline Bouvier and John Kennedy talking at their wedding in 1953. Her relaxed pictures were different from stiff wedding portraits.
How is a relaxed picture different from a posed one?
Kennedy Wedding: Jackie Throwing the Bouquet
Toni Frissell photographed Jackie Kennedy throwing the wedding bouquet in 1953. Guests reached up to catch it.
Why do brides throw bouquets?
Jazz Festival
John Vachon photographed a jazz festival for Look magazine in 1954 in Rhode Island. The Newport Jazz Festival began that year.
What instruments are in a jazz band?
Geoffrey Holder and Carmen de Lavallade
Carl Van Vechten photographed the dancers Geoffrey Holder and Carmen de Lavallade in 1955. They were a famous dance couple.
How do two dancers move together?
Beauty Parlor, Washington, D.C.
Warren K. Leffler photographed a beauty parlor in Washington, D.C., in 1957. Women sit under dryers and wait for their hair to set.
What would you do under a hair dryer?
X-15 Attitude Control Studies at Langley
NACA, the agency that became NASA, photographed a simulator at Langley in 1958 used to study how to control the X-15 rocket plane. Pilots practiced with machines before flying.
Why practice on a simulator?
Photographer Warren K. Leffler on a Flight Deck
Warren K. Leffler, a U.S. News and World Report photographer, stands on the flight deck of an aircraft carrier in 1959. His camera is slung at his side.
What would you photograph on a carrier?
Marilyn Horne and Henry Lewis
Carl Van Vechten photographed opera singer Marilyn Horne and conductor Henry Lewis in 1961. They later married.
What instruments does an opera need?
James Meredith Walking
Marion S. Trikosko photographed James Meredith, the first Black student at the University of Mississippi, in 1962. U.S. marshals escorted him on campus.
What would it be like to be the first?
John Lewis Leading a Civil Rights March
David S. Johnson photographed John Lewis and others leading a large civil rights march in the early 1960s. Lewis became a congressman.
Why do people march together?
Justice Byron White
Marion S. Trikosko photographed Byron Whizzer White, Supreme Court justice, in 1962. He had been a football star.
How can an athlete become a judge?
Titov and Glenn at the White House with Kennedy
Marion S. Trikosko photographed Soviet cosmonaut Gherman Titov and American astronaut John Glenn at the White House with President Kennedy in 1962. They were two of the first space travelers.
What would you ask an astronaut?
Fuller Brush Salesman Visiting a Home
Marion S. Trikosko photographed a Fuller Brush salesman visiting a home in 1962. Door-to-door salesmen sold brushes and household goods.
How is shopping different today?
Hecht Company Rental Service
Marion S. Trikosko photographed the rental service at the Hecht Company department store in Washington in 1962. Customers could rent clothes and equipment.
What would you rent?
Fannie Lou Hamer, Hattiesburg, Mississippi
Danny Lyon photographed Fannie Lou Hamer in a civil rights march in Hattiesburg, Mississippi, in 1962. Hamer became a leader in the fight for Black voting rights.
Why was voting so hard to win?
The March on Washington, August 28
Danny Lyon photographed the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom on August 28, 1963. Roughly 250,000 people came to demand civil rights and jobs.
Why would 250,000 people travel to one place?
Katherine G. Johnson at Work
This photograph shows Katherine G. Johnson at her desk at NASA. She was a mathematician who calculated the orbits for John Glenn's flight and for the Apollo moon missions.
How could a person calculate an orbit by hand?
Bomb Wreckage near the Gaston Motel
Marion S. Trikosko photographed the wreckage near the Gaston Motel in Birmingham, Alabama, after a bombing in 1963. The motel was a headquarters for civil rights leaders.
Why would someone attack a motel?
A. Philip Randolph and Other Civil Rights Leaders
Marion S. Trikosko photographed A. Philip Randolph and other civil rights leaders in the Capitol rotunda in 1963 during the March on Washington. They met with senators to push for a civil rights law.
Why would leaders meet with lawmakers?
Aerial View of the Crowd and Stage, March on Washington
Marion S. Trikosko photographed an aerial view of the crowd at the Lincoln Memorial on August 28, 1963. The huge crowd stretches along the Reflecting Pool.
What does a crowd look like from above?
Passengers Including Nuns, Union Station
Marion S. Trikosko photographed passengers, including nuns, walking near trains at Union Station in Washington in 1963. Thousands of marchers came by train.
How would you travel to a big event?
Conferring on the Civil Rights March
Leaders confer in New York about the plans for the March on Washington in 1963. An Associated Press photograph shows serious men around a table.
How would you plan a huge march?
Marchers Leave for Washington
Marchers board buses in New York in 1963 to go to the March on Washington. Thousands of buses and trains carried them.
What would you bring on a long bus ride?
Marchers in the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom
Flip Schulke photographed marchers at the March on Washington on August 28, 1963. People held signs demanding jobs and freedom.
What would you want to say in a march?
March on Washington
Bruce Davidson photographed the March on Washington in 1963. Davidson, a documentary photographer, caught the hopes of the crowd.
What do you see on people's faces?
March on Washington, Crowd at the Washington Monument
Bruce Davidson photographed the crowd gathering at the Washington Monument for the March on Washington. The monument rises above the marchers.
Why would marchers meet at the monument?
Mother, Father and Son at the March on Washington
David S. Johnson photographed a family at the March on Washington in 1963. Many families brought children.
Why would parents bring a child to a march?
Tired Marchers
A White House news photographer photographed tired marchers resting after the March on Washington in 1963. Their feet were sore after a long day.
How would your feet feel after a march?
Civil Rights Hootenanny
A White House news photographer photographed a civil rights hootenanny, a folk music gathering, in Washington in 1963. Singers like Joan Baez and Bob Dylan sang at the march.
What songs would you sing at a march?
Charter Planes Arriving at National Airport
Thomas O'Halloran photographed charter planes arriving at National Airport in Washington for the Civil Rights March in August 1963. Marchers came from all over the country.
How many planes can you count?
Civil Rights March on D.C.
Thomas O'Halloran photographed the civil rights march in Washington on August 28, 1963, for U.S. News and World Report. The crowd fills the Mall.
How do you picture a crowd of 250,000?
Firemen Turn Hoses on Protesters, Birmingham

Bruce Davidson photographed firemen turning high-pressure hoses on civil rights protesters in Birmingham, Alabama, in 1963. Police also used dogs, and the pictures shocked the nation and helped lead to the Civil Rights Act.
How can pictures change people's minds?
Equal Rights in '63 Buttons
David S. Johnson photographed demonstrators wearing buttons that said Equal Rights in '63 at the March on Washington. The buttons show how people stated their cause.
What would you put on a button?
Crowd at the Washington Monument
David Lowell Johnson photographed the crowd at the Washington Monument during the March on Washington in 1963. People wait in the shade of the trees.
What would you do waiting in a crowd?
Marchers Holding Signs
David Lowell Johnson photographed people holding signs and marching during the March on Washington in 1963. Signs asked for jobs and an end to segregation.
What words on a sign are the most powerful?
Signs at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool
David Lowell Johnson photographed people holding signs at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in 1963. The marchers gathered near the water.
What do the signs say?
Crowd at the Lincoln Memorial
David Lowell Johnson photographed the crowd gathered at the Lincoln Memorial during the March on Washington in 1963. Martin Luther King Jr. gave his I Have a Dream speech from the steps.
What would you do if you heard that speech?
Washington March
Stanley Tretick photographed the March on Washington for Look magazine in 1963. Marchers fill the grass in front of the monument.
How does a photographer cover a huge march?
Russell Jones, Civil Rights Activist from Ohio
Roosevelt H. Carter photographed Russell Jones, a civil rights activist from Ohio, at the March on Washington in 1963. Carter was a Black photographer from Columbus.
Why would a photographer from Ohio go to the march?
People Marching Beside Parked Buses
Roosevelt H. Carter photographed marchers beside parked buses in Washington in 1963. Buses carried marchers from across the country.
How long might the bus trip have taken?
Lady at the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom
Roosevelt H. Carter photographed a woman at the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom and the Emancipation Proclamation centennial in 1963. She wears her best clothes.
Why would she dress up for a march?
Martin Luther King Jr. Delivers His Address at the Lincoln Memorial
The Rev. Martin Luther King Jr. gave his I Have a Dream speech at the Lincoln Memorial on August 28, 1963. His words about freedom and equality are among the most famous in American history.
What is your dream for the world?
James L. Farmer Jr.
Marion S. Trikosko photographed James L. Farmer Jr., a civil rights leader and founder of the Congress of Racial Equality, in 1964. CORE organized the Freedom Rides.
What do the Freedom Riders do?
Senate Civil Rights Debate
Howard Brodie sketched and photographed the Senate gallery during the civil rights debate in 1964. The Senate debated the Civil Rights Act for months.
Why would a law take months to pass?
30,000 Civil Rights Marchers in Montgomery
An estimated 30,000 civil rights marchers fill the street in front of the Alabama State Capitol in Montgomery in March 1965. They had walked from Selma over several days.
How far would you be willing to walk for a cause?
Selma to Montgomery March
James Karales photographed marchers on the Selma to Montgomery civil rights march in Alabama in 1965. The marchers walked 54 miles to demand voting rights.
Why was voting so important?
Duke Ellington and Ella Fitzgerald Performing
John Vachon photographed jazz musician Duke Ellington and singer Ella Fitzgerald performing together in 1966. They were two of the greatest names in jazz.
What makes jazz special?
Young Men Who Have Been Drafted Wait in Line
Warren K. Leffler photographed young men who had been drafted waiting in line to be processed in Columbia, South Carolina, in 1967. During the Vietnam War, young men were drafted into the army.
How would you feel if you were drafted?
Edward Moore Kennedy
Yousuf Karsh photographed Senator Edward Kennedy in 1968. He was the youngest brother of John and Robert Kennedy.
What would it be like to follow two famous brothers?
President Nixon Tossing Out the First Pitch
Warren K. Leffler photographed President Richard Nixon throwing out the first baseball at the Washington Senators' opening game in 1969. Presidents often throw a first pitch.
Could you throw a first pitch?
Saturn V Carrying Apollo 11

A Saturn V rocket carrying astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin Aldrin lifts off on July 16, 1969, to begin the first mission to land people on the Moon. The rocket was taller than the Statue of Liberty.
How loud do you think the launch was?
Apollo 12: Surveyor III and the Lunar Module
Apollo 12 astronauts photographed the Surveyor III spacecraft and their lunar module on the Moon in November 1969. Surveyor III had landed there two and a half years before.
How did astronauts find an old spacecraft on the Moon?
Alan Bean on the Moon
Pete Conrad photographed astronaut Alan Bean next to the lunar module on the Moon in November 1969. Bean later became a painter of moon scenes.
What would you paint if you had walked on the Moon?
Buzz Aldrin at the Lunar Landing Research Facility
Astronaut Buzz Aldrin practices at the Lunar Landing Research Facility at NASA Langley. The giant frame hung machines to feel like the Moon's lower gravity.
How could you practice for low gravity?
Edward Bennett Williams
Marion S. Trikosko photographed Edward Bennett Williams, a famous Washington lawyer, in 1970. He was also the owner of the Baltimore Orioles.
What does a lawyer do for a sports team?
Washington Senators Baseball Team on the Field
Marion S. Trikosko photographed the Washington Senators baseball team standing on the field in 1971. The Senators left Washington after that year.
Why would a team leave a city?
Artist's Concept of Apollo 15 Crew Deploying the Lunar Rover
NASA made this artist's concept of the Apollo 15 crew setting up the lunar roving vehicle in June 1971. The rover let astronauts travel miles across the Moon.
Why would astronauts need a car on the Moon?
Downtown of an Old Mining Town, Bisbee, Arizona
Cornelius Keyes photographed the downtown of Bisbee, Arizona, in 1972 for the EPA's DOCUMERICA project. Bisbee was a copper mining town in the hills.
How would a mining town differ from another town?
Copper Mines and Smelter, Inspiration, Arizona
Cornelius Keyes photographed the Inspiration Consolidated Copper Company's mines and smelter in Arizona in 1972. Smoke rises from the plant above the desert.
How do you separate metal from rock?
A New Mechanical Trash Collection Method
Cornelius Keyes photographed a new mechanical trash collection method sponsored by the Environmental Protection Agency in 1972. Trucks replaced manual pickup.
How do you think a machine can pick up trash?
Ghost Town, Bodie, California
Dick Rowan photographed Bodie, a gold-mining ghost town in eastern California, in 1972. The empty buildings stand as people left them.
Why do people leave a town?
The Tiger Coal Shovel, Hanna Coal Company
This photograph from 1972 shows a huge coal shovel called The Tiger working at a strip mine of the Hanna Coal Company in Ohio. Such shovels were among the largest machines on land.
How big would a shovel need to be to dig coal like that?
Aerial of Phoenix, Arizona
Cornelius Keyes photographed Phoenix, Arizona, from the air in 1972 for DOCUMERICA. The city spreads across the desert in a grid.
How does a city in a desert differ from one by the sea?
Oregon's Prehistoric Rain Forest Park
Gene Daniels photographed a park in Oregon with giant ferns and moss in 1972 for DOCUMERICA. The park, actually called Prehistoric Park, looks like a dinosaur-era forest.
What would you expect to see in a rain forest?
Bank Vault in the Ruins, Bodie
Dick Rowan photographed a bank vault standing in the ruins of an old bank at Bodie, California, in 1972. The thick vault door survived while the building around it fell.
Why would the vault survive?
A Bulldozer Prepares a Path for a Coal Shovel
A bulldozer clears a path for one of the huge coal shovels in Ohio in 1972. The bulldozer looks tiny.
How can a machine make another machine look small?
A Coal Shovel Works into a Hillside near Cadiz, Ohio
A giant coal shovel works into a hillside off Route 9 near Cadiz, Ohio, in 1972 as part of the DOCUMERICA project. Strip mining changed the land.
What happens to a hillside after strip mining?
Impeach Nixon
A demonstrator holds an Impeach Nixon sign in Washington, D.C., in 1973 during the Watergate scandal. The nation was in turmoil over the break-in at the Democratic headquarters.
Why would people want to remove a president?
The House of Coal, in Front of City Hall, Cadiz, Ohio
A sculpture called The House of Coal stands in front of the city hall of Cadiz, Ohio, in 1973. The town celebrated its coal heritage.
What does a town want to show off?
Golda Meir
Marion Trikosko photographed Golda Meir, the prime minister of Israel, in 1973. Meir was one of the first women to lead a country in the modern era.
What does it take to lead a country?
Heavily Tagged Subway Car in New York
Erik Calonius photographed a New York City subway car covered in graffiti in 1973. Street art began on the subways in the 1970s.
Is graffiti art or vandalism?
Caribbean Harbor
John Vachon photographed a Caribbean harbor in 1973 for the EPA's DOCUMERICA project. Boats float near a shoreline of houses and palms.
What do boats in a harbor need?
Bayamón Housing Development
John Vachon photographed a housing development in Bayamón, Puerto Rico, in 1973 for DOCUMERICA. Rows of houses show how the city grew.
What do planned neighborhoods look like?
Landfill at Bayonne, New Jersey
Hope Alexander photographed a landfill at Bayonne, New Jersey, on New York Bay in 1974 for DOCUMERICA. Trash was buried and covered with earth.
What happens to trash over time?
Alistair Cooke
Marion S. Trikosko photographed Alistair Cooke in 1974. Cooke was a British-American broadcaster who hosted Masterpiece Theatre.
What would you ask a TV host?
